laws.rule: In the City of Cork it is an offence to drink alcohol on a street or in a public place (open spaces, river banks, parks and green spaces) in the council's area. It is also an offence to hold alcohol in an opened can, opened bottle, opened pack or a glass or cup while on a street or in an open space intending to drink it there; the bye-laws presume that intent unless the person shows otherwise. The fine on conviction in the District Court is up to EUR 2,500 (about A$3,973 at RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293) (Cork City Council bye-laws, paragraphs 2 to 4, as commenced in January 2022). Drinking at tables and chairs a hotel, restaurant or pub provides next to it, within its licence and licensed hours, is not an offence (paragraph 5). Any member of the Garda is an authorised person.
